Chapter 8: The Burden and Blessing of Bearing Witness.
Let’s be honest—bearing witness is never easy.
As her journey deepened, she realized she was carrying more than just her own pain. She felt the weight of others’ stories too. Some days, it was almost too much—a heaviness in her chest that made it hard to breathe.
But alongside that weight, there was something else. A sense of purpose. By telling the truth, she knew she was honoring people who’d been denied justice.
She thought back to a quiet moment with her cousin, who once admitted he’d always been afraid to ask about their grandfather. “I didn’t want to make things worse,” he whispered. And she got it. We usually avoid tough questions—sometimes out of love, sometimes out of fear, or just wanting to protect ourselves and the people we care about.
But here’s something important: silence, in its own way, can cause harm too.
In choosing to bear witness, she found both a burden and a blessing. She learned to hold space for grief, to listen without judgment, to offer comfort even when there weren’t any easy answers. She started to see how simply acknowledging pain could change everything—how it could turn shame into pride, or fear into courage.
Of course, there were moments of doubt. Times when the sheer size of the task nearly overwhelmed her. But each time she shared her story, she noticed something: the load felt a little lighter. She felt a bit more whole.
It dawned on her that healing isn’t about forgetting. It’s about remembering in a new way—about discovering meaning, even in the middle of loss.
Most people don’t realize just how powerful it can be to bear witness—to say, “I see you. I hear you. Your story matters.”
For her, this simple truth became a guiding light. It helped her keep moving forward, even when the way ahead was anything but clear.
